authority: explicit user instruction to make extracted Weighted/Log BRC tools and theorems part of the foundation for all research, with subsequent main-backed recurrent results returned through the same Foundation backflow rule
purpose: Expose only minimal typed branch/recurrent commitments universally; detailed theorem IDs, examples, successful routes and tool catalogs remain lazy and must not choose a free research question.
commitments: BRANCHING_IS_TYPED: Boolean support, positive weighted multiplicity/mass, provenance, and signed/amplitude data are distinct carriers unless an explicit reduction theorem identifies them.

DECLARED_MULTIPLICITY_IS_NOT_DEFAULT_DISCARDABLE: when a problem itself declares multiple branch representatives and their multiplicity or positive weights matter, do not silently collapse them to Boolean support before testing what is lost.

POSITIVE_WEIGHTED_BRANCH_MINIMAL_CARRIER: for finite positive-rational branch families the shared exact summary available to research is CWM=(C,W,M), carrying supported path count, total positive mass, and dominant path mass.

LOG_IS_DERIVED: E=W/M and Delta=LN(E) are derived readout coordinates for live positive CWM states; LN/LOG are not primitive native state and need not be materialized during exact branch accumulation.

FINITE_RATIONAL_RECURRENCE_CERTIFIED: for any finite non-negative rational transition-mass matrix W, total all-depth positive mass is stable iff there exists a positive rational potential h with Wh<h; after denominator clearing this has an exact positive integer certificate, and the complementary divergent phase has an exact nonzero non-negative integer left certificate.

RECURRENT_GAUGE_LOCALIZATION: finite rational mass stability is equivalent to a positive rational state gauge in which every outgoing total-mass row sum is strictly below one; closed-cycle products are gauge-invariant.

RECURRENT_LOOP_INVARIANTS_AVAILABLE: when finite positive rational recurrence is actually present, exact determinant/zeta, recurrent response, criticality and feedback-condensation interfaces are part of the shared Foundation; floating spectral values are not required primitive state.

RATIONAL_GAUGE_HAS_INTEGER_COORDINATES: positive rational multiplicative gauge/holonomy should preserve exact prime-valuation coordinates before optional logarithmic readout; mod-m skeleton and rational thickness are separately typed.

FEEDBACK_INTERACTION_IS_HIGHER_ORDER_TYPED: simultaneous positive feedback updates may have cooperative recurrent interactions of arbitrary finite order; pairwise edge responses/interactions are not assumed complete. Exact event-level condensation and all-orders subset interactions are available when the problem declares a finite feedback set.
SIGNED_BOUNDARY: positive Weighted-BRC does not encode signed/amplitude cancellation or reflection-odd orientation after positive recoalescence.

DETERMINISTIC_DEGENERATION: a single deterministic positive path has C=1, W=M, E=1 and Delta=0; the weighted layer contributes no extra multiplicity information and should not be forced onto deterministic problems.
BOOLEAN_BASE_PRESERVED: canonical R023 Boolean result-support BRC remains the base support semantics and is not mutated by the weighted layer.

RECURRENT_SCOPE_BOUNDARY: current recurrent/interaction Foundation covers finite non-negative rational positive-mass systems only; do not extrapolate to infinite state spaces, signed/amplitude recurrence, complex weights, or arbitrary non-rational exact weights without a separate theorem.

phase_a_anti_anchoring.rule: These commitments are background typing rules, not a research agenda. FREE Phase A must still generate its own question from the primitive substrate and may open detailed Weighted-BRC theorem/tool surfaces only after the self-generated problem actually contains the relevant typed branch/recurrent structure.
forbidden: presenting weighted/recurrent BRC theorem IDs as suggested research questions
preloading successful arithmetic/selector/holonomy/recurrent/feedback examples to steer question choice
forcing multiplicity, recurrence or feedback interpretations onto deterministic or signed problems
